exposure: socioeconomic status (education, subjective status location, financial possibilities)
outcome: need for medical treatment (infections, gestational diabetes, threat of premature birth)
rated care and support during pregnancy and birth
cohort: The study included mothers living in Austria who participated in an online cross-sectional survey.
finding: A lower socioeconomic status is associated with adverse health outcomes during pregnancy and childbirth, as well as diminished satisfaction with healthcare.
mod_finding: A low assessment of financial opportunities was found to be associated with an increased number of labour inductions and caesarean sections.
